scientific_decision: NO-GO: the 2026 author paper already accounts for changing heavy/light membership and database-size thresholds by amortized rebalancing. A distinct online data-dependent epsilon policy was not shown to provide a useful migration-accounted improvement.
confirmed_increment: Reconstructed Theorem 11 and the full major/minor rebalancing argument from arXiv:2605.08397v1; corrected the prior C5 premise that dynamic skew itself was untreated.

gate_results.uncovered_gap: partial: online instance-sensitive epsilon selection is distinct, but no performance objective or theorem-level advantage established

strongest_candidate_blocker: Any policy must maintain exact Q(D_t) during threshold transition and charge rebuilding, delta dual-maintenance or log replay, peak old/new materialized state, and enumeration delay. No causal comparator, stream class, or strict gain over the query-optimal fixed-epsilon maintenance-width baseline was specified/proved.
naive_policy_falsifier: Alternating states that trigger complete threshold rebuilds can incur preprocessing-scale O(N^(1+mw)) cost per switch; this refutes rebuild-on-every-switch only, not all possible migration schemes.
